FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
On an entrance ramp the entering driver speeds up and yields to interstate traffic, while on an exit ramp the driver slows only after reaching the deceleration lane [A01].
Why it matters: group ramps; difficulty medium; prereq sec10-F04; confusables sec10-F05, sec10-F07
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A02
Passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the interstate requires a lane change where safe, and only when no lane change is possible does the rule become slowing to twenty miles per hour under the limit [A02].
Why it matters: group move over on interstates; difficulty high; prereq sec10-F16; confusables sec10-F16, sec10-F11
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A02
A missed exit is handled by continuing to the next one, never by backing up on the interstate and never by using the emergency crossover [A02].
Why it matters: group interstate rules; difficulty low; prereq sec10-F14; confusables sec10-F14, sec10-F10
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A03
Passing on the right is lawful on a multilane road or beside a vehicle turning left, but never by leaving the pavement or the main traveled part of the road [A03].
Why it matters: group passing rules; difficulty medium; prereq sec10-F18; confusables sec10-F24, sec10-F25
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A02
A yellow line on your right on a divided highway warns you are going the wrong way, whereas the correct position puts white on the right and yellow on the left [A02].
Why it matters: group markings; difficulty low; prereq sec10-F17; confusables sec10-F17, sec10-F11
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0052]
